summary.headline: Aegis Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 212% YoY to INR545 crore and normalized EBITDA 184% to INR727 crore, driven by a record LPG distribution quarter.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q1 FY27 results, with PAT of INR545 crore (up 212% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR727 crore (up 184%). The Gas division posted its highest-ever EBITDA of INR591 crore (up 296% YoY), with distribution volumes of 2.77 lakh MT (up 91% YoY, up 19% QoQ). Liquids EBITDA rose 28% to INR136 crore on INR178 crore revenue. Management announced several port and capacity milestones, including commissioning of a 36,000 MT ammonia terminal at Pipavav and a Board-approved 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA.

segments.name: Gas (LPG) – Logistics
segments.commentary: Throughput held steady at 1.124 million MT. Sourcing volumes rose marginally 1% YoY to 1.21 lakh MT.

segments.name: Gas (LPG) – Distribution
segments.commentary: Record 2.77 lakh MT volume. Management cites a distribution margin of INR7,000+ per MT as sustainable, versus INR4,000 historically.

segments.name: Liquids
segments.commentary: Highest-ever Q1 EBITDA of INR136 crore, with five consecutive quarters of EBITDA growth. Mangalore liquid capacity of 193,000 CBM is fully utilized after a 75,000 CBM addition.

guidance_outlook: Cumulative capex of about $1.2 billion targeted in FY27.
Capex pipeline of about $5 billion through FY2030-31; funding via equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting gearing of about 0.6.
Distribution volume: management aims for 2 million MT, now expected to cross 1 million MT this year and possibly 1.5 million MT next year; growth rate closer to 50% per management.
Logistics throughput: worst-case growth of about 25% a year, with step-up growth possible as Pipavav and KGPL enablers are used.
Mumbai 64,000 CBM liquid storage (INR125 crore) targeted for commissioning in H1 FY27.
JNPA first phase of about 100,000 CBM liquid storage targeted for Q3 FY27; Kochi additional 49,577 CBM expected early next fiscal year; Kandla CRL 4 (94,148 CBM) targeted next year.
capex_capacity: Mumbai: 334,000 CBM liquid and 21,000 MT static LPG; 64,000 CBM expansion under way.
JNPA: 101,900 CBM liquid today; about 318,100 CBM liquid, 77,236 MT LPG and a 35,000 MT bottling plant under a roughly INR1,675 crore program. Board also approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank.

Pipavav: LPG capacity now 70,800 MT after a 48,000 MT terminal commissioned June 2025; 36,000 MT ammonia terminal commissioned; VLGC-compliant jetty due this year; liquid rail gantry with 0.5 million MT/yr take-or-pay due by year-end; Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline connection expected in H1 FY27. Jamnagar-Loni LPG pipeline complete.
Kandla: 952,000 CBM liquid and 48,000 MT LPG; VLGC-compliant; CRL 4 expansion targeted next year.
Kochi: 82,545 CBM liquid today, rising to 132,122 CBM after a 49,577 CBM addition.
Mangalore: 82,000 MT LPG terminal commissioned June 2025; LPG rail gantry and bottling plant at INR52.5 crore; liquid capacity 193,000 CBM; evaluating 60,000 CBM more.
Haldia: about 25,000 MT LPG terminal under HPCL terminaling agreement to 2038; 226,890 CBM liquid storage; 3 acres of land acquired for expansion.
Vadhavan port: non-binding MoU for a potential INR20,000 crore investment, subject to approvals.
demand_pricing: Management says distribution volume growth reflects new customers, wider geography and ullage added from Pipavav and Mangalore cryogenic terminals, not only the war.

Blended distribution margin was about INR7,000/MT in FY26 and Q1 FY27. Management says the margin should be INR7,000+ going forward, supported by shipping savings from VLGC carriers (freight of about $15 vs $50 on MGCs).
Management states margins were not INR5,000 in Q4 or Q1 and said blended FY margin matters more than quarterly figures.
Ammonia: distribution to industrial customers starts within weeks of commissioning; no cylinders or gas stations. Margins not disclosed.
Management says it is a distributor, not a trader, and does not take inventory or price positions.
Morbi demand has partly restarted; management says Morbi is no longer the core of the business.
Logistics tariffs are uniform across ports; no port-wise split given.

qa_highlights.question: Is distribution volume growth ahead of expectations, and are the customer contracts sticky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2 million MT aim predates the war and reflects infrastructure build-out; new cryogenic terminals at Pipavav and Mangalore have added ullage and geography.

qa_highlights.question: How should EBITDA per ton be viewed near term and structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR7,000+ per MT is sustainable. It expects the margin not to fall back to INR4,000, citing procurement gains from VLGC shipping as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the per-unit margins for sourcing, logistics and distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquids EBITDA is divided by capacity (about 2 million CBM). Logistics throughput gives close to INR1,000/MT EBITDA. Sourcing is a low contributor, at about $85-90/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth outlook beyond 25% CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: 25% is the benchmark for logistics; anything above depends on the enablers. Distribution growth is expected to be higher, closer to 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why not fill more storage given the ITOCHU partnership and the LPG supply deficit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not take inventory or price positions and will distribute on a monthly basis, rather than act as a trader.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash across subsidiaries fund the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: AVTL is self-funded through equity, and ITOCHU is planned to rise to 25% over three years. Standalone cash is around INR2,700 crore, and consolidated liquidity exceeds INR5,940 crore. Management will hold cash until it finds opportunities.
